ble_219_0c04bd98.name: sdp_get_service_record_handle
ble_219_0c04bd98.summary: Read the 32-bit ServiceRecordHandle (attribute 0x0000) of an SDP record, 0 if absent
ble_219_0c04bd98.description: Looks up attribute 0x0000 (ServiceRecordHandle) in the record's attribute list with sdp_record_find_attribute (0x0c04cb6c). It then requires the value element to be a UINT-type data element of 32-bit size (two small predicates at 0x0c04c578 and 0x0c04c570, whose exact meaning is inferred from the return values 1 and 2) and returns the big-endian u32 payload read at element offset 1 with co_read32_be. Returns 0 when the attribute is missing or has the wrong type. sdp_register_service treats any value below 0x10000 as an invalid handle, so 0 is the failure signal. Part of the SDP record-access group (sdp_record_find_attribute, sdp_record_matches_pattern, sdp_record_attribute_list_length, sdp_record_write_attribute_list).

params.name: param_1
params.description: SDP service record, DE-encoded attribute list

params.name: param_4
params.description: pass-through to co_read32_be, which ignores it

returns.description: ServiceRecordHandle value, or 0 if not found or not a 32-bit UINT

ble_219_0c04bd98.notes: The packet callee list names bthost_byte_get_low3_bits and bthost_byte_get_high5_bits, but the decompiled body does not call them; the calls are to 0x0c04c578, 0x0c04c570, 0x0c04cb6c and co_read32_be.

ble_219_0c04bdc8.name: sdp_register_service
ble_219_0c04bdc8.summary: Register an SDP service record: validate its handle, reject duplicates, link it into the list
ble_219_0c04bdc8.description: Reads the record handle with sdp_get_service_record_handle and returns 0x83 (invalid handle) when it is below 0x10000. It walks the global record list at 0x2000fcb4 and returns 0x80 (already registered) when a record with the same handle exists. Otherwise it takes a 12-byte service_record_item_t from btstack_memory_service_record_item_get (8-entry pool), stores the handle at item+4 and the record pointer at item+8, and pushes the item on the list head with btstack_linked_list_add. Returns 0x56 when the pool is exhausted and 0 on success. Registration only; removal is not in this function. Members of the SDP record-table group: sdp_server_build_service_search_response, sdp_server_build_service_attribute_response and sdp_server_build_service_search_attribute_response all walk the same list.

params.name: param_1
params.description: DE-encoded SDP service record, stored by pointer (not copied)

returns.description: 0 on success, 0x83 invalid handle, 0x80 duplicate handle, 0x56 no free item

ble_219_0c04bdc8.notes: Status code names follow BTstack sdp_server.c; the exact code-to-name mapping is inferred.

ble_219_0c04be10.name: sdp_server_build_service_search_response
ble_219_0c04be10.summary: Answer an SDP ServiceSearchRequest with the matching record handles
ble_219_0c04be10.description: Parses the request PDU: transaction id at +1, ParameterLength at +3, ServiceSearchPattern DE sequence at +5, MaximumServiceRecordCount u16 right after the pattern, then a continuation-state byte (0, or length 2 followed by a 16-bit resume index). It finds registered records that match the pattern (sdp_record_matches_pattern over list 0x2000fcb4) and writes a ServiceSearchResponse into the global response buffer 0x2000fb98: PDU id 3, transaction id, ParameterLength, TotalServiceRecordCount, CurrentServiceRecordCount, then one raw 32-bit handle per returned record. The count is capped by MaximumServiceRecordCount and by the response budget (roughly (MTU-12)/4 handles); when records remain, a 2-byte resume index is appended as continuation state. Malformed requests return 0 and produce no response. Group: the three SDP request handlers (here, sdp_server_build_service_attribute_response, sdp_server_build_service_search_attribute_response) share the record list and response buffer.

params.name: param_2
params.description: response budget (the ATT/L2CAP MTU of the channel)

returns.description: length of the response PDU in 0x2000fb98, 0 if the request is malformed

ble_219_0c04bfd0.name: sdp_server_build_service_attribute_response
ble_219_0c04bfd0.summary: Answer an SDP ServiceAttributeRequest for one record handle and an attribute id list
ble_219_0c04bfd0.description: Parses the request: transaction id at +1, ParameterLength at +3, ServiceRecordHandle u32 at +5, MaximumAttributeByteCount u16 at +9, AttributeIDList DE sequence from +0x0b. If the handle does not match a record in list 0x2000fcb4, it writes an ErrorResponse (PDU 1) with error 0x0002 (Invalid Service Record Handle). Otherwise it writes a ServiceAttributeResponse (PDU 5): transaction id, ParameterLength, AttributeListByteCount, then the id/value list produced by sdp_record_write_attribute_list cut at the byte budget. The continuation state is 0 when the list completed, or 2 followed by a 16-bit resume offset when it did not. Returns the total PDU length, or 0 for a malformed request. Member of the SDP request-handler group with sdp_server_build_service_search_response.

returns.description: length of the response PDU in 0x2000fb98, 0 if malformed

ble_219_0c04c144.name: sdp_server_build_service_search_attribute_response
ble_219_0c04c144.summary: Answer an SDP ServiceSearchAttributeRequest with attribute lists for all matching records
ble_219_0c04c144.description: Parses the request: ServiceSearchPattern at +5, MaximumAttributeByteCount u16 after it, AttributeIDList after that, then a continuation-state field. For a fresh request it first sums the encoded size of each matching record's attribute list (sdp_record_attribute_list_length, plus 3 bytes per record for its sequence header) and stores that total in the AttributeListsByteCount field at 0x2000fb9f. It then emits one attribute list per matching record with sdp_record_write_attribute_list, resuming from the continuation state when one is present and stopping at the budget (MTU minus 12, capped by MaximumAttributeByteCount). The response is ServiceSearchAttributeResponse (PDU 7) with transaction id, ParameterLength, AttributeListsByteCount, the lists, and a continuation trailer. Malformed requests return 0. Member of the SDP request-handler group.

returns.description: length of the response PDU in 0x2000fb98, 0 if malformed

ble_219_0c04c144.notes: The continuation-state layout (4 bytes: record index and byte offset) is inferred from the code that reads two u16 values at +1 and +3.

ble_219_0c04c680.name: sdp_pattern_uuid_match
ble_219_0c04c680.summary: Per-UUID callback for a ServiceSearchPattern: fail unless the record contains the UUID
ble_219_0c04c680.description: Invoked by de_traverse_sequence for each element of a ServiceSearchPattern, with the candidate record as context. A DE_UUID element with 16-, 32- or 128-bit payload is normalised to a 128-bit UUID (uuid_add_bluetooth_prefix for the short forms) and searched for in the record's attribute values with de_traverse_sequence and the comparator at 0x0c04c978. If found, it returns 0 so the traversal continues. If not found, or if the element is not a UUID, it clears the result flag at context+4 and returns 1, which stops the traversal and fails the match. Net effect: a record matches only if every UUID in the pattern occurs in it. Used only by sdp_record_matches_pattern.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pattern element (DE header followed by UUID bytes)

params.name: param_4
params.description: context: [0] = service record pointer, [1] = match result flag

returns.description: 0 = UUID found, continue; 1 = not found or not a UUID, stop

ble_219_0c04c780.name: sdp_attribute_write_fragment
ble_219_0c04c780.summary: Per-attribute callback: write one attribute id and value into a byte-budgeted SDP response
ble_219_0c04c780.description: Callback used by sdp_record_write_attribute_list through sdp_attribute_list_traverse_sequence, once per (id, value) pair in a record. It first checks whether the id is in the requested attribute id list (param_5[3], matched with de_traverse_sequence and the comparator at 0x0c04c528). For a matching attribute it emits the 3-byte id element (DE_UINT16 header 0x09 plus the big-endian id), then copies the value element with memcpy, honouring a resume offset and the bytes still allowed by the budget. The state struct tracks output pointer, skip count, bytes written and bytes remaining. Returns 1 when the budget ran out part-way through (the traversal stops and a continuation is needed) and 0 when the attribute finished or was not requested. Write half of the SDP attribute serializer; the length pass is sdp_attribute_add_length.

params.name: param_5
params.description: write state: [0] output pointer, [1] skip/offset count, [2] bytes written, [3] attribute id list, [4] remaining budget

returns.description: 1 = budget exhausted mid-attribute, 0 = done or not requested

ble_219_0c04c780.notes: The state-struct field meanings are inferred from the arithmetic and the traversal call; word offsets are approximate.

ble_219_0c04c89c.name: sdp_attribute_add_length
ble_219_0c04c89c.summary: Per-attribute callback: add 3 + value length to the running attribute-list size
ble_219_0c04c89c.description: Callback used by sdp_record_attribute_list_length through sdp_attribute_list_traverse_sequence. For an attribute id that is in the requested id list (*param_5, matched with de_traverse_sequence and the comparator at 0x0c04c528), it adds the value element length from de_get_len plus 3 bytes for the DE_UINT16 id element to the 16-bit running total stored at param_5+4. It always returns 0 so the traversal continues. This is the sizing pass that runs before sdp_record_write_attribute_list writes the bytes.

params.name: param_5
params.description: [0] requested attribute id list, [1] low 16 bits = running byte total

returns.description: always 0 (continue)

ble_219_0c04cb10.name: sdp_record_write_attribute_list
ble_219_0c04cb10.summary: Serialize the requested attributes of an SDP record into a byte-budgeted, resumable buffer
ble_219_0c04cb10.description: Wrapper around sdp_attribute_list_traverse_sequence that walks the record's attribute list and applies sdp_attribute_write_fragment (0x0c04c780) to each entry. The arguments give the record, the attribute id list, a resume offset, a byte budget, an out-parameter for the number of bytes written, and the output buffer. It returns 1 when the whole list fit and 0 when the traversal stopped at the budget, in which case the caller writes a continuation state. Callers are sdp_server_build_service_attribute_response and sdp_server_build_service_search_attribute_response.

params.name: param_3
params.description: resume offset within the record's attribute list

params.name: param_5
params.description: out: u16 number of bytes written

returns.description: 1 = whole list written, 0 = stopped at the budget

ble_219_0c04cb48.name: sdp_record_attribute_list_length
ble_219_0c04cb48.summary: Total encoded size of the requested attributes of an SDP record
ble_219_0c04cb48.description: Returns the number of bytes that sdp_record_write_attribute_list would emit for the attribute id list param_2 on record param_1. Each matching attribute contributes its 3-byte id element plus the length of its value element. The sum is accumulated by sdp_attribute_list_traverse_sequence with the callback sdp_attribute_add_length (0x0c04c89c), so the result is a 16-bit total. Used to fill the AttributeListsByteCount field before the bytes are written.

returns.description: encoded byte count of the matching attributes

ble_219_0c04cb6c.name: sdp_record_find_attribute
ble_219_0c04cb6c.summary: Find an SDP record attribute by 16-bit id and return a pointer to its value element
ble_219_0c04cb6c.description: Walks the attribute list of record param_1 with sdp_attribute_list_traverse_sequence and the id comparator at 0x0c04c518, and returns the value element for attribute id param_2. Returns 0 when the record has no such attribute. Used by sdp_get_service_record_handle with id 0x0000. Member of the SDP record-access group.

returns.description: pointer to the value data element, or 0

ble_219_0c04cb90.name: sdp_record_matches_pattern
ble_219_0c04cb90.summary: Return true when an SDP record contains every UUID of a ServiceSearchPattern
ble_219_0c04cb90.description: Walks the ServiceSearchPattern DE sequence param_2 with de_traverse_sequence and the per-UUID callback sdp_pattern_uuid_match (0x0c04c680), using the record as context. The result starts at 1 and is cleared by any failing element, so the function returns true only when every UUID in the pattern is present in the record, which is the BTstack ServiceSearchPattern rule. Used by all three SDP request handlers to select records.

returns.description: true if the record matches the whole pattern

ble_219_0c04ceb8.name: att_server_handle_request
ble_219_0c04ceb8.summary: Decode one ATT request PDU and build its response (MTU, discovery, read, write)
ble_219_0c04ceb8.description: The ATT server request dispatcher: it switches on the request opcode at *param_2 and writes the response PDU into param_4, returning its length or 0 for no response. Exchange MTU (0x02) sets the negotiated MTU to max(23, min(client MTU, server MTU)) in param_1[1]. Find Information (0x04), Find By Type Value (0x06), Read By Type (0x08) and Read By Group Type (0x10) walk the attribute database at 0x2000fcb8 with att_iterator_fetch_next and the UUID matchers, emitting uniform-length entries; group types 0x2800 and 0x2801 drive the grouping. Read (0x0a), Read Blob (0x0c) and Read Multiple (0x0e) check READ permission through att_validate_security and copy values with att_copy_value. Write Request (0x12), Prepare Write (0x16), Execute Write (0x18) and Write Command (0x52) work only on dynamic attributes (flag 0x100) and call the write callback at 0x2000fccc with modes 0 write, 1 prepare, 2 commit, 3 cancel and 4 pre-check; prepared-write state lives at 0x2000fcbc..0x2000fcc4. Any other opcode gets an Error Response with code 0x06 (Request Not Supported).

params.name: param_1
params.description: ATT connection context: [1] negotiated MTU, [2] server MTU, flags

returns.description: response PDU length, 0 when no response is sent

ble_219_0c04ceb8.notes: Attribute flag bits used: 0x02 read, 0x04 write without response, 0x08 write, 0x100 dynamic (callback-backed), 0x200 128-bit UUID. Error-code mapping follows the ATT spec; the exact per-branch error codes were not all verified. This function is a dispatcher and is part of the ATT server group with att_server_write_callback.

ble_219_0c04def0.name: att_event_forward_class4
ble_219_0c04def0.summary: Forward an ATT server event to the hook dispatcher under hook class 4

params.name: param_4
params.description: event payload pass-through (also passed as the fifth argument)

ble_219_0c04dfb8.name: att_server_write_callback
ble_219_0c04dfb8.summary: ATT write callback: persist CCC bonds, broadcast commit/cancel, dispatch to attribute handlers
ble_219_0c04dfb8.description: Registered as the ATT write callback (0x2000fccc) by att_server_init, and called with a mode in param_3. Modes 2 (commit) and 3 (cancel) broadcast to every entry of the handler list at 0x2000fcf8 and then to the application callback at 0x2000fcec. Mode 4 (pre-check) does the same but returns the first non-zero status. Modes 0 (write) and 1 (prepare) find the list entry whose handle range covers the attribute handle and call its callback, falling back to the application callback. For a plain 2-byte write to a persistent Client Characteristic Configuration (att_is_persistent_ccc), it also stores the CCC value through the bonding storage callbacks: up to 20 tag slots with keys 0x42544300 plus the slot index ('BTC' plus index), each 8-byte record holding a counter, handle, bond index and tag. Store failures are logged as 'att_server.c:%u: Store tag index %u failed' (lines 0x3b0 and 0x3d1).

params.name: param_1
params.description: connection context (passed to the handlers as the connection handle)

params.name: param_3
params.description: mode: 0 write, 1 prepare, 2 execute/commit, 3 cancel, 4 pre-check

params.name: param_4
params.description: write offset (0 for a plain write)

returns.description: 0 = accepted, otherwise an ATT error code

ble_219_0c04dfb8.notes: The mode meanings are inferred from how att_server_handle_request calls the callback. The 8-byte CCC storage record layout is inferred from the stores and reads, and the storage callback table layout (read, write, delete) is inferred.

ble_219_0c04eb24.name: att_server_init
ble_219_0c04eb24.summary: Initialise the ATT server: GATT database, read and write callbacks, hook and event subscriptions
ble_219_0c04eb24.description: Called once from ble_219_0c059230. It stores the application context (param_2) at 0x2000fce8 and the application callback (param_3) at 0x2000fcec, registers the class-4 sink with ble_sink_init (0x0c04ded8 with 0x0c04e399), installs the compiled GATT database through att_set_db (0x0c04cdf0), and registers the read callback 0x0c04e295 through att_set_read_callback. Finally it sets the ATT write callback at 0x2000fccc to att_server_write_callback (0x0c04dfb9). Two hook pointers (0x2000fcf4 and 0x2000fd00) are set to the same handler at 0x0c04e6fc.

ble_219_0c04f634.name: sm_device_db_resolve_peer
ble_219_0c04f634.summary: Match a peer against the LE device DB by address and IRK and report its slot
ble_219_0c04f634.description: Identity-resolves the peer of the connection record param_1. With flag bit 2 of 0x2000ff59 set, it walks the device DB slots (count from le_device_db_tlv_max_count, identity from le_device_db_tlv_read_identity) and compares the stored 16-byte IRK words at 0x20010128..0x20010134 and the 6-byte address at 0x20010149. When the address type at 0x20010148 is zero it scans for an address match instead. If no slot matches, it inserts the entry with le_device_db_tlv_add. On success it sends link frame 0xD3 (address pair and slot index) through ble_link_notify_pair_addrs, sets the connection state byte at +0x0b to 3, and stores the slot index at +0x18. When the key-flag bytes on the connection and flags 0x2000ff6c, 0x2000ff59 indicate it, it also writes encryption info with le_device_db_tlv_set_encryption. Part of the SM identity-resolution path with sm_pairing_step_complete.

params.description: connection record: u16 handle at +0, state at +0x0b, DB index at +0x18, key flags at +0x19..+0x23

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c050700.name: sm_pairing_step_complete
ble_219_0c050700.summary: Advance the per-link pairing state machine when one pairing or encryption step completes
ble_219_0c050700.description: Completion handler for one SM step. param_1 == 1 means success, anything else failure. It takes the pending link from global 0x2000fd84 and clears the pending step code at 0x2000fd8c and the saved timer handle at 0x2000fd90. If a pending link exists with step code 2, it sets the link state byte at +0x15 among the encoded pairing states 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x1D, 0x1E and 0x20, and runs the local/identity notifications (ble_link_notify_local, ble_link_notify_id_addr) or the cleanup helpers, depending on the state and on flags 0x2000ff35 and link+0x03. On success it publishes an 11-byte frame 0xCE (handle, state byte from 0x2000fd7a, 6-byte address copied reversed with co_reverse_copy_6) through ble_evt_publish. On failure it sends frame 0xCF through ble_link_notify_pair_addrs. Pairing-state group with sm_device_db_resolve_peer and sm_link_poll_state.

ble_219_0c050700.notes: The meanings of the encoded state values 0x1B to 0x20 and of the step codes are inferred from the transitions, not from a spec. The packet does not show the caller of the state change.

ble_219_0c052b50.name: sm_init
ble_219_0c052b50.summary: One-time SM initialisation: run-loop timer, event handlers, default constants, key tables

ble_219_0c052c7c.name: sm_link_poll_state
ble_219_0c052c7c.summary: Periodic SM poll for the current connection: re-check its identity record and re-arm the timer
ble_219_0c052c7c.description: Looks up the connection record (ble_ctrl_conn_find_by_handle, handle passed in r0) and returns if none is found. ble_219_0c053f74.name: ble_app_queue_message
ble_219_0c053f74.summary: Frame an app/UART message and queue it, splitting it when it exceeds the frame limit

ble_219_0c0581a8.name: ble_random_static_addr_build

ble_219_0c058208.name: ble_link_table_write_at18
ble_219_0c058208.summary: Copy up to 24 bytes into the current link entry at offset 0x18 and commit
ble_219_0c058208.description: Gets the current link table entry from ble_link_table_get_base (0x0c059558, table base 0x200134BC), copies param_2 bytes from param_1 to entry+0x18 with memcpy, and calls ble_219_0c059754 (not described in this packet) to commit the change. Returns 0x41 without copying when the length is 0x19 or more, so the field holds at most 24 bytes.

returns.description: 0 on success, 0x41 when the length is out of range

ble_219_0c05822c.name: ble_link_table_write_at0
ble_219_0c05822c.summary: Copy up to 24 bytes to the start of the current link entry and commit
ble_219_0c05822c.description: Same as ble_link_table_write_at18 (0x0c058208) except that the copy destination is the start of the entry returned by ble_link_table_get_base, not offset 0x18. It also calls ble_219_0c059754 to commit, and returns 0x41 for a length of 0x19 or more.

returns.description: 0 on success, 0x41 when the length is out of range

ble_219_0c0582b0.name: ble_event_window_expire
ble_219_0c0582b0.summary: Expire old entries of the 10-slot event ring and count them into two tallies
ble_219_0c0582b0.description: Works on a ring of ten 27-byte records: a flag byte at offset 0 (value 9 marks one event kind, anything else the other) and a 32-bit timestamp at offset 0x13. The reference time is the monotonic clock (FUN_0c03feac with id 4, when param_1 is 0), otherwise the timestamp of the record at the head index 0x20013235. Starting at the tail index 0x2001311F, it walks entries that are at least 300 time units older than the reference. Each expired entry increments the tally at 0x2001322F (flag 9) or 0x200130FC (other), records the first expired timestamp in 0x20013230 or 0x20013100, and decrements the pending count at 0x20013234. It stops at the first younger entry and commits the new tail index. Only caller: ble_219_0c0585a4.

params.name: param_1
params.description: 0 = use the current clock as the reference; otherwise use the head entry timestamp

returns.description: none

ble_219_0c0582b0.notes: The 300 threshold unit is presumably milliseconds. The meaning of the two tallies is not established from this function alone.
